newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, but price direction seen down.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, but price direction seen down.

text.p: Asian crude prices were slightly firmer on Monday, supported by the wider global futures price, although wet trading was quiet.
A major bid April Oman at MPM less five cents per barrel, reflecting some sentiment that MidEast grades will trade at a discount in April.
Traders said they expected most MidEast grades to achieve premiums initially but then drift in what is expected to be a weak demand month featuring ongoing run cuts and turnarounds.
Late deals on March Murban --late last week-- were done at flat to ADNOC, reflecting the general weakness in the grades.
The expected weakness is likely to make Dubai-related trades active, partly for sellers to avoid showing deals done at a discount to the OSP.
High ADNOC and Oman differentials against Dubai are adding to the bearish sentiment hanging over the MidEast market.
One trader said much of the initial direction would depend on the action of Japanese term buyers and whether they look to aggressively sell barrels they do not want into the spot market.
In the regional market, traders were still waiting for the release of Indonesia's export allocations covering March for trading to begin in earnest.

Traders said Bach Ho term talks were settled at quotes plus 80 cents per barrel for April to September. That raises the term price 17 cents from the previous six-month period, although spot deals have been 60 to 70 cents above OSP.
Traders were reasonably mixed on the outlook for Australian grades while Cossack has halved production to 40,000 bpd.
With Griffin due to be shut down for six weeks Maintenance from April 1, some players believe there could be a squeeze on March and April liftings.
